beats.text: One spouse earns a hundred and twenty thousand, the other thirty thousand. Same ten thousand dollar RRSP deposit. Whose name it's in changes the tax.
Alex puts ten thousand into a spousal RRSP. Alex claims the deduction, from Alex's own room, and saves about three thousand nine hundred and fifty dollars.
Years later, Sam takes the ten thousand out. At Sam's lower income, the tax at today's rates is about two thousand four hundred and eighty dollars. Roughly fifteen hundred less.
The trap: if Sam withdraws while Alex contributed this year or in the two years before, it's taxed to Alex. About four thousand three hundred and forty dollars.
The twist: the rule counts calendar years. One deposit in December can tie up the plan for three tax years.
Time withdrawals around the last contribution, and check with an accountant before taking money out.
Next: pension income splitting. How retired couples move income on paper. Follow so you don't miss it.
